A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToMiE research, despite the revised title. Their complete main texts and included appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on DNA-Rendering and ZJU-MoCap, component ablations, and animation demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Motion Kernel/LBS ablations, skinning-weight visualizations, and training-time and rendering-speed results.

M1.justification: The hybrid Motion Kernel/LBS assignment, gradient-based joint growth, joint-position and rotation MLPs, non-rigid correction, and training procedure remain unchanged. Replacing 'modular growth' with 'adaptive growth' and introducing 'exoskeleton' terminology do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight DNA-Rendering sequences covering handheld objects and loose clothing, plus tight-clothing cases from ZJU-MoCap. The added analyses and dress-animation example remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated rendering baselines remain 3DGS-Avatar, GART, GauHuman and Im4D. Im4D imagery is regrouped in v2 Figure 9. Although Figure 5 removes GART's animation panels, its fixed-body animation comparison remains described in Section 5.5.

E3.justification: v2 introduces MK-only and LBS-only experimental controls and a comparison of training to convergence and rendering FPS on a single RTX 3090. Existing DNA-Rendering settings retain 24 training views, six test views, 100 frames, and the same image-quality metrics and masking procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix D, Table 6 and Figure 11 add a targeted test of whether combining Motion Kernels and LBS improves rendering and joint localization over either alone. Appendix C/Figure 10 adds skinning-weight inspection. The original joint-growth and non-rigid ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added average timing results do not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: 3DGS-Avatar scores change for DNA sequences 0007_04, 0041_10 and 0800_07; its aggregate full-image PSNR changes from 27.69 to 28.93 without an accompanying explanation of changed settings. ToMiE's existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. New Tables 6–7 report component-ablation and efficiency results, including ToMiE's 30-minute training time and 60+ FPS; Figure 5 adds a dress-animation example.

T1.justification: Equation (3) corrects the transmittance product from factors containing alpha_i to factors containing alpha_j, so it uses the preceding Gaussians' opacities. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: adaptive SMPL skeleton extension, hybrid gradient assignment, and explicitly controllable joint optimization for rendering and animation. The new title and clothing/object terminology do not materially broaden these claims.

C2.justification: v2's Table 1 caption and Appendix I interpret Im4D's LPIPS advantage through its lack of SMPL constraints while identifying color distortion as a PSNR weakness. Table 2 explicitly qualifies ToMiE's ZJU-MoCap performance as comparable in SSIM/LPIPS and superior in PSNR. The existing topology-change limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly identifies the single GeForce RTX 3090 used for the efficiency comparison, and Table 7 supplies training times and rendering speeds. Previously documented MLP sizes, initialization, 8,000 warm-up iterations, growth thresholds, densification settings and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 add focused comparisons with auto-rigging, clothing simulation, SMPLicit and rendering-only approaches, with new references such as RigNet, SNUG, HumanRF and 4K4D. These clarify differences in required inputs and explicit controllability while retaining the paper's central positioning.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises portions of the abstract and introduction, and consistently replaces broad 'garments' terminology with handheld objects and loose clothing. Appendix subsections A.1–A.6 become separately lettered sections with additional analyses; the main section sequence and most technical prose remain.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 2 is redrawn, Figures 4 and 8 exchange main-text/appendix roles with revised panels, Im4D comparisons are regrouped into Figure 9, and Figure 5 removes GART panels and adds dress animation. The combined benchmark table is split, and new Tables 6–7 and Figures 10–11 expand the displayed evidence.

improvement.justification: The new Motion Kernel/LBS ablation supplies direct quantitative and localization evidence for an existing design choice, while efficiency measurements improve practical assessment. Broader related-work comparisons and the Equation (3) correction also help. Removing GART's animation panels weakens the immediate visual comparison, although the discussion remains. Overall, these are useful but bounded gains; the method and principal benchmark conclusions are unchanged.
